workflow_runs.display_title: Fix CI: it was failing on every run, for two independent reasons

head_commit.message:
Fix CI: it was failing on every run, for two independent reasons

The workflow had never passed. All 8 runs since it was added were red. I
had only replicated the steps by hand locally and assumed that was
enough; it was not, and I should have checked the actual run status
before claiming the project was ready.

Cause 1 - inline heredocs do not work on Windows runners
- Steps used `python - <<'PY' ... PY` inside `run: |`. The default shell
  on windows-latest is pwsh, which has no heredoc support, so those
  steps could never work there. Worse, the heredoc terminators were
  mis-indented inside the YAML block, so they were broken on Linux too.
- Fix: every check is now a real file under tools/ and CI just calls
  `python tools/<check>.py`. Portable across shells.
  New: tools/validate_skills.py, tools/check_scaffolds.py,
       tools/check_dist.py

Cause 2 - PyYAML was assumed to be preinstalled
- The frontmatter step did `import yaml` with a comment claiming PyYAML
  ships on GitHub runners. It does not (it is not in the stdlib, and the
  dependency step only installed numpy). That is exactly where the
  ubuntu-latest jobs died.
- Fix: `pip install ... numpy PyYAML`, and validate_skills.py falls back
  to regex-based checks with a printed warning if PyYAML is missing, so
  the check degrades instead of crashing.

Also fixed while here
- check_scaffolds now asserts the 3D/2D file split, not just that the
  scaffold exits 0: a 2D project must not receive FirstPersonController
  or EnemyAI (they need Physics/AI built-ins), and a 3D project must not
  receive PlatformerController2D. Both directions verified.
- check_dist verifies the four upload zips exist, since that is the path
  upload-based hosts actually use.
- check_toolchain reads Blender from $BLENDER then PATH with a fallback,
  instead of a hardcoded Windows path that would fail on the Linux runner.
- Scaffold/dist temp dirs are gitignored.

Verified locally, each exiting 0: compileall, gate unit tests,
validate_skills, check_scaffolds, check_dist, check_toolchain (8/8).
The real test is whether the next CI run goes green, which I will check.

workflow_runs.name: CI
workflow_runs.display_title: Add an end-to-end toolchain check, fix stale README claims

head_commit.message:
Add an end-to-end toolchain check, fix stale README claims

Audited the repo as a sceptical first-time user rather than re-reading
my own code. Two real problems found.

1. Both READMEs claimed 2D "controllers must be rewritten" - stale the
   moment PlatformerController2D landed in the previous commit. A user
   reading that would not know a controller ships with the kit. Both
   languages corrected, and the line now also states what is still
   genuinely missing (2D navigation uses grid A*, not NavMesh).

2. The gates had only ever been proven piecemeal: exit codes in one
   place, silhouette IoU in another. Nothing asserted the actual
   *decisions* the README promises.

New: tools/check_toolchain.py
- Builds fixtures from scratch, runs every shipped gate, and asserts
  the documented behaviour rather than just "it ran":
    topology pass / unapplied-transform reject / missing-file exit 2
    silhouette match PASSes with IoU >= 0.85
    wrong-proportioned FAILs
    a typo'd flag exits 2 instead of silently skipping the gate
    a misspelled --stage errors
    turntable still renders 4 views
- Measured: 8/8 pass, IoU 0.9935 for the matching asset and 0.3546 for
  the wrong one - consistent with what the README states.
- Reads the Blender binary from $BLENDER, then PATH, then a fallback.
  Hardcoding one machine's path would have broken CI and everyone else;
  verified both the env-var and fallback paths work.
- Wired into the CI blender job, so the decision-quality of the gates,
  not merely their exit codes, is now enforced on every push.

Also checked and found clean: every C# type referenced in docs exists in
code; documented reference paths resolve (two apparent misses were
cross-skill references to files that do exist); the three gate numbers
quoted in the README (0.85/0.05 thresholds, 15% tolerance cap, 48px
short-side floor) all match the source exactly.

workflow_runs.name: CI
workflow_runs.display_title: Add 2D platformer controller and fix the 2D scaffold generating 3D files

head_commit.message:
Add 2D platformer controller and fix the 2D scaffold generating 3D files

2D had documentation but no code. Now it has a controller, and the
scaffold no longer produces a project that cannot compile.

New: PlatformerController2D.cs
- Rigidbody2D-based, matching the approach references/11-2d-gameplay.md
  prescribes. The 3D template's CharacterController cannot be used here.
- Coyote time (0.10s) and jump buffer (0.10s). These two are the
  difference between "jump feels sticky" and "jump feels right"; most
  hand-rolled 2D controllers omit them and then the game feels cheap.
- Variable jump height (release truncates ascent), ground check via
  Physics2D.OverlapCircle rather than collision normals, continuous
  collision detection so fast falls do not tunnel through floors.
- Uses Rigidbody2D.linearVelocity. Verified against the real engine
  metadata: Rigidbody2D.velocity does not exist in Unity 6 - it was
  renamed, and the old name is absent from the assembly entirely. Code
  copied from older tutorials will not compile.

InputReader: expose JumpAction (read-only)
- JumpPerformed only reports the press moment; variable jump height
  needs to know whether the button is still held. Rather than have the
  controller guess, the reader exposes the action null-safely.

Fix: --dimension 2d generated a project that does not compile
- Found by actually building one. 2D mode installed com.unity.2d.* but
  still emitted the 3D-only files, and a 2D project typically does not
  enable the Physics or AI built-in modules:
    CS1069 'CharacterController' forwarded to UnityEngine.PhysicsModule
    CS1069 'NavMeshAgent' forwarded to UnityEngine.AIModule
- copy_tree now filters by dimension: 2D skips seven 3D-only files
  (FirstPersonController, PlayerLook, EnemyAI, EnemyPerception,
  Interactor, InteractableBase, PickupItem), 3D skips the 2D controller.
- Verified both ways: 2D emits 17 files, 3D emits 22, no cross
  contamination.

Verified in a real editor
- 2D project compiles in Unity 6000.0.84f1 with zero CS errors,
  emitting G2D.dll (36864 bytes) and G2D.Tests.dll (5632 bytes).
- Re-confirmed the documented two-run flow: first pass reports the
  InputSystem GUID as missing, second pass after the package downloads
  backfills it and the build goes green - same behaviour as the 3D path.

SKILL.md and CHANGELOG updated to describe the controller and the
dimension split.
